what_it_does: loads entity tables and attaches relationship columns, copying the entity frame once per edge

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The .assign result is bound to source_eblock, which is not read again and is not stored back. Whether the earlier column writes reach the frame depends on pandas semantics that were not checked here, so the repair must keep those writes. Not measured.

what_it_does: downloads, gunzips and parses the dataset descriptor on every access

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Every read re-downloads the descriptor, while detail_describe and visualize_info just above cache theirs. Caching the parsed descriptor on the instance removes the repeats. Network-bound.

what_it_does: derives the assay mapping from the descriptor, rebuilt on each access

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The mapping is a function of the descriptor and is recomputed on every access. It is cheap next to the download, so the saving comes mainly from the descriptor cache in the unit above.

what_it_does: returns the assay names, evaluating assays_info_dict twice

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: assays_info_dict is evaluated in the if test and again in the for iterable, and each evaluation is a full descriptor download. One local serves both.

what_it_does: adds an entity-field filter to a cohort payload, converting stored values with a caller-supplied reduce lambda

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The lambda is a parameter supplied by the caller, and it defines how each stored value is converted. The quadratic copy lives inside the caller's lambda, and replacing the reduce here would drop that conversion, which changes the function's contract. Not a repair of this unit alone.

what_it_does: opens and parses a schema file that is never used, because the schema validation call is commented out

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: json_schema is read and parsed at 296-297 and read nowhere else; the only use is a commented-out validate call. Removing the read removes a file open and a json parse per call. Behaviour changes only when the schema file is missing, where the function would no longer raise; the measured inputs use the shipped file.

what_it_does: describes the project and fetches a bin file, probing a file id first and falling back to a dx cat subprocess

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The project is described on every call, and somatic_filter_payload calls retrieve_geno_bins up to three times per query. Only project_desc['region'] is used, so a cache of region per project removes the repeats. Network-bound.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The describe at 23 is the probe that selects the staging-manifest branch by raising ResourceNotFound. Dropping it changes which branch runs, so it is an existence check, not discarded work.

what_it_does: checks that each item of a list is a string, testing the Python version once per item

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: python_version is a module constant, so the comparison at line 31 repeats per item for no reason. Hoisting it out of the loop leaves the result unchanged. Expected to measure as negligible.

what_it_does: checks that each item of a list is a string, testing the Python version once per item

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The same loop-invariant python_version test at line 15, in the somatic copy of the helper. Expected to measure as negligible.

what_it_does: validates infer flags and builds an error message string that is used only on the error path

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The f-string with three str().lower() conversions is built on every call and read only inside the two error branches. Moving it into those branches removes the work on the common path. Expected to be negligible per call.

what_it_does: builds the payload for a filter, loading one of four return-column JSON files on every call

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The return-column file is opened and parsed on each call, though its content is fixed. The module already loads column_conversion.json once at import, so loading these at import matches it. Saves a file open and a parse per call; expected modest.

what_it_does: rewrites a genotype SQL statement to add the return columns missing from its select list

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: return_columns_genotype.json is opened and parsed on each call. Its content does not change, so one load at module level serves every call. Provided the loaded list is not mutated by _harmonize_sql_select_named_expression; that was not checked and the measured check covers the outputs.

what_it_does: downloads a database file in one part, describing the database and hashing every chunk

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: dxdatabase_desc is assigned from a describe call and never read; the parts list is rebuilt locally at 186. Removing the describe saves one API round trip per download. Network-bound.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: hasher is created and fed every chunk, but its only reader, verify_part, is commented out at 256 and 266, so the digest is never used. Removing the hashing removes a full MD5 pass over the file. Output bytes are unchanged.

what_it_does: returns a cached download URL, checking object existence in the project before the cache test

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: object_exists_in_project issues a describe before the cache check at 193, so the describe repeats on every chunk even while the URL is cached. Moving the cache test first skips the describe on cache hits. Matches dxfile.py, which keeps the check inside the cache-miss branch.

what_it_does: returns the description of the underlying workflow for a region, with a cache that never hits

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Line 194 stores the whole workflow description dict in self._workflow_desc_by_region, whose keys are field names, so the region test at 181 never matches and every call repeats the describes. Storing the result under the region key makes the cache answer. Network-bound.

what_it_does: returns a handler for the underlying workflow of a region, with a cache that is never written

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: _workflows_by_region is read at 215 and never written in this module, so the lookup always misses and describe runs each call. Line 226 stores a handler in the wrong attribute and line 227 builds the same handler again. Writing the handler to _workflows_by_region fixes the cache. Network-bound.

what_it_does: downloads a file part by part, hashing each part even when it has no md5 to compare against

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For a part without an md5 key the hasher created at 494 is fed every chunk at 497, but verify_part never compares that digest. Skipping the hasher for those parts removes the hashing. Applies only to parts without md5, which the code does not say how often occur.

what_it_does: buffers writes and flushes full buffers, recursing with the unsent remainder of the data each time

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each buffer-full recurses with data[remaining_space:], copying everything still unsent. A write of N bytes into buffers of B bytes copies about N squared over 2B. A loop over offsets copies each byte once. The TODO at 530 names the same concern. Network-bound: write_request uploads, so the generator is expected to fail.

what_it_does: yields lines of a file read in large chunks, splitting each chunk into a full list before yielding its first line

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: parts = _buffer.split('\n') builds a list of every line in each chunk before the first is yielded, and the list is dropped after the chunk. A generator that scans for newlines yields each line without the list. Network-bound: read() calls the server.

what_it_does: mounts job inputs with dxfuse, starting subprocesses for mkdir and id

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: os.makedirs and os.getuid/os.getgid would replace the subprocesses, but subprocess mkdir raises CalledProcessError on an existing directory and makedirs raises FileExistsError. A caller that catches the first would see a different exception type, which the contract forbids.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The find walk prints the mount tree to stdout, so its output is part of what the job log shows. Removing it changes printed output, which the contract covers.

what_it_does: downloads named paths, listing a project's folders for each path argument

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: list_subfolders fetches the full project folder list and filters it locally to the one name that matches abs_path. list_folder(folder=parent_folder, only='folders') returns only the direct subfolders and is already used in cp.py. Network-bound.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The project folder listing is requested inside the per-path loop, so each path argument refetches it. Fetching it once per project before the loop serves all paths.

what_it_does: checks that every output row has the same column names before writing the rows

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The all() generator rebuilds set(COLUMN_NAMES) for every row, although COLUMN_NAMES is fixed before the loop. Building expected = set(COLUMN_NAMES) once and comparing i.keys() against it gives the same check.

what_it_does: updates a workflow stage, fetching the workflow's edit version before the no-op early return

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: dxworkflow.editVersion at 213 triggers a describe on a fresh handler, but initial_edit_version is read only at 263, after the early return at 220-224. Moving the read after the early return skips the describe when no update is requested. Network-bound.

what_it_does: resolves a path to a project and id, reading the extended attributes of one path twice when FUSE is in use

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: xattr(path) is called twice in one expression. One local serves both reads. Runs only when _DX_FUSE is set, so the measurement may not reach it.

what_it_does: resolves job output references by describing each element of a job output array

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: One describe request per element of the output array. dxpy.describe accepts a list and makes one bulk call. Network-bound.

what_it_does: resolves a list of paths, describing ID paths one at a time while name paths are sent in one bulk call

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each ID path costs one describe inside the loop, while name paths are gathered into one resolve_data_objects call at 1012. Gathering ID paths the same way removes the per-path requests. Network-bound.

what_it_does: resolves job-based object references in a job's inputs, describing the producing job once per distinct field

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The cache key includes the field name, so two outputs of the same job each trigger a full job describe. Caching the job description by job id serves every field. Network-bound.

what_it_does: archives the resources directory, checks for an existing bundle with the same checksum, and uploads a new one if none exists

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The whole tar is built before the checksum lookup decides reuse, and the tar is discarded when a bundle exists. The checksum depends only on names, modes and mtimes, so a metadata pass could decide reuse first. This is a restructure of the function rather than one line, so it may not reduce to a single measured repair.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The uncompressed tar is re-read and gzipped into a second file. A tarfile 'w:gz' stream would produce the same members but a different gzip byte stream, so the uploaded file's bytes change. The contract covers the files written.

what_it_does: checks that every executable of a workflow is enabled in the requested regions, describing each stage's executable

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The executables list keeps one entry per stage, so a shared executable is described once per stage that uses it. A dict keyed by executable id, filled once, serves all stages. Network-bound.

what_it_does: checks a Python file's syntax by writing a bytecode file and deleting it again

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: compile() in memory would skip the file write, but it raises SyntaxError where py_compile raises PyCompileError, so the exception type seen by the caller changes. The contract forbids that, and mapping the error back is not a one-line repair.

what_it_does: checks the suggestions of each input, describing a project and an object for each one

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: project_describe(suggestion['project']) runs once per suggestion, though the answer depends only on the project id. One lookup per distinct project serves all of them. Network-bound.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: dxpy.describe of a file or record binds the full result, which the code never reads; only the 404 check matters. A describe with a fields restriction keeps the check and drops the payload. Network-bound.

what_it_does: builds an app locally, uploading resources to each enabled region

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: project_describe(working_project, region) runs at 793-794, and the same describe runs again at 845-846 for dest_project, which is the same project. Reusing the first result removes one API call. Network-bound.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: upload_resources is called once per region and archives the directory each time. Archiving once would need upload_resources to take a prepared archive, which changes its signature and contract, so no single-unit repair exists here.

what_it_does: waits on each depends_on id, describing data objects before waiting for them to close

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe at 210 is inside the try whose except re-raises as 'Could not wait for ...'. It can fail for a missing or inaccessible object, so it decides the error path. Removing it changes what the caller sees.

what_it_does: walks the job input JSON and records each file input's handler and name

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: handler.name is a lazy describe per file, so each file input costs one describe request. A single bulk describe of all input ids would supply the names. Network-bound; the repair changes how the handlers are created, so it may need more than one line.

what_it_does: builds an asset bundle by uploading inputs and starting an app job

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: system_whoami() is an authentication probe. When credentials are bad, the outer except prints the error and exits 1; without the probe a later call fails with a different message and possibly after uploads have started. Changing the failure path is not a waste-only edit.

what_it_does: truncates a log message so its JSON encoding fits in 8000 characters, dropping one byte per pass

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop removes one byte per pass and re-runs json.dumps over up to 8000 bytes each pass, so the number of passes equals the excess of the escaped encoding over the limit. The length of the JSON encoding is non-decreasing in the prefix length, so bisection finds the same largest prefix in about 13 probes. Same output for every input.

what_it_does: suggests a correction for a word from a list of known words, computing the one-edit candidates again for the two-edit search

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: _edits1(word) is computed for the one-edit test and again inside _known_edits2 when that test finds nothing. Computing it once and reusing it inside correct gives the same candidate set. The module has no callers in src/python, so the effect on this repository is nil; the measurement is on the function itself.

what_it_does: lists app names matching a prefix for tab completion, calling find_apps on each keystroke

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: find_apps runs on every completion request with no stored listing, so each TAB repeats the same API call for the same name class. Storing the listing on the completer serves repeats. Network-bound.

what_it_does: collects path completions by searching data objects once per class

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: find_data_objects takes one classname per call, and the results must be kept per class, so no single request answers all the classes. The per-class calls are required by the API shape, not avoidable waste.
